statement: Rubin Ultra chip-level power is reported at approximately 1800W for the mainstream Max-Q variant, with a possible Max-P variant at 2600W to 2800W and a lower-power 1200W variant for token decoding, within an NVL576 scale-up of eight racks of 72 GPUs each.
why: Per-chip power climbing toward and past 2 kilowatts means data center electrical and cooling capacity, not chip availability, increasingly decides how many accelerators can be switched on.

impact.mechanism: Higher power per accelerator raises the electrical and cooling load per rack, so existing data center shells and grid connections support fewer chips, throttling deployable supply.

evidence.excerpt: Chip-level power consumption is 'approximately 1800W' for the mainstream Max-Q variant; a possible Max-P variant at '2600W-2800W'; and a lower-power variant at '1200W' for workloads like token decoding.

confidence.basis: Secondary aggregator citing SemiAnalysis; not confirmed by NVIDIA and the Max-P variant is described as only possible.

dispersion: The document gives watts per chip, not performance per watt, so no efficiency value is recorded; the Max-P figure is a 2600W to 2800W range.
